paper.title_en: Finite-wavelength corrections to dynamical friction in fuzzy dark matter: a causal linear-response approach
paper.abstract_en: A massive body moving through fuzzy dark matter (FDM) generates a density wake whose gravitational backreaction produces dynamical friction. We investigate how finite-wavelength effects modify this force using causal linear-response theory and the statistical Wigner formulation. For a homogeneous Maxwellian background and general isotropic finite-size perturbers, we derive an analytic representation of the gravitational drag and recover the classical Chandrasekhar result under matched regularization conditions. In the controlled semiclassical regime, the leading finite-wavelength correction is quadratic in $\hbar/m_χ$ and factorizes into a velocity-dependent function and a ratio of spectral moments characterizing the source structure. Remarkably, this correction reduces the drag magnitude independently of the detailed radial source profile within the adopted Maxwellian model. Gaussian and exponential sources illustrate this result. We further establish a controlled remainder bound and clarify the nonuniform behavior of the point-source limit. These findings identify the physical conditions under which wave effects modify classical dynamical friction.
